comments.text: Three-byte packed-decimal score, least significant byte first. Award/subtract helpers change this target; $11-$13 holds the displayed score that catches up to it.
Three-byte packed-decimal score shown in the six status digits. The score update moves it toward $0B-$0D by up to two decimal units per call.
Address of the next raster interrupt body. The hardware IRQ entry at $196A banks in I/O and jumps through this word; $1975 installs the next body from X/Y.
Low byte of the display tick counter. The display handler increments it while the pause flag is clear; timed animation compares saved values with this byte.
High byte incremented when the low display tick counter wraps.
Room number used to select room-specific geometry, records and callbacks. Several selectors reject values eight and above before indexing the eight-room lists.
Index selecting the controlled character in the parallel character state tables. Initialization selects zero; character-change code toggles it.
Latest active-low joystick-port-2 sample, read from $DC00 by the display handler.
Previous active-low joystick sample, copied from $4B before the next sample is taken.
Accumulated newly pressed joystick bits. The display handler combines old/new active-low samples into active-high press bits and ORs them into this byte.
Horizontal facing selector used when sprite offsets are added to or subtracted from the player's world X coordinate.
Player action-state number. The dispatcher at $8CD1 doubles it and jumps through the word table at $8CE2.
Step within an action sequence. The movement sequence at $9AE2 advances it by two, with action-specific termination checks.
Low byte of player world X, combined with $5E. The shape renderer offsets it to place component sprites.
Player vertical coordinate used when the shape renderer computes sprite Y positions.
High byte of player world X, combined with $5C.
Candidate low world X coordinate. At the end of the mechanics calls, the main loop resets it from the current position at $5C for the next iteration.
Candidate high world X coordinate paired with $61.
Candidate player Y coordinate. The main loop resets it from the current Y coordinate at $5D after its mechanics calls.
First of the four zero-page collision-list pointers selected by the shared list helpers. The part's room setup supplies their addresses.
Current four-byte collision-record pointer. The shared scans advance it by four until the first byte is $FF, and copy a successful record address to $A5/$A6.
A nonzero value suppresses the display handler's game-tick work. The main loop sets it during pause and clears it when fire resumes play.
